notes: RBox revision of functionality: capital_of (tagged functional: a city is the national capital of at most one country) loses it. Replaces the earlier edit on enclave_within: its direct question was missed by 2 of 4 models (Rule 6), and reviewers flagged that functionality of 'is an enclave within' is the word's definition and that the instances (Lesotho in Botswana, San Marino in France) are ruled out by geography, so 'no' stayed fair after the edit. Every model answered the old near query ("Can one city be the national capital of two different countries at the same time?") correctly, so this property is held. Functionality of capital_of follows from no other tag of it (inverse:has_capital, subproperty:located_in, chain:located_in->located_in). geography-replace-0012 edits a different property of the same relation (its subproperty). The instance questions ask what the given fact rules out or allows, "given only this", so the answer rests on the fact and the property rather than on the known capitals of Germany and Greece. Yes and no: the first instance (and the cross-lingual queries) asks whether the fact rules out a second country (yes, then no), the second whether a second country is possible (no, then yes). Near asks the same property of 'is the largest city of' (reference no, differs from the new yes). Far changed from 'is a cousin of' (missed by 3) to 'is a colleague of'. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
